issues.legal_issue: Compensation for acquired land must reflect its market value at the time of the acquisition notification and cannot be increased merely because the land was later developed and sold at a higher price.
material_facts: The land was treated as agricultural, and no evidence showed that it had non-agricultural potential or that the owners suffered special damage.
The owners produced no comparable sale near the notification date or other evidence supporting their claimed higher value.
They relied on later sales of developed land at a much higher price and on a High Court determination of value for land in the same village acquired under the same notification.
The Court adopted that High Court determination and enhanced the market value from Rs. 6,500 to Rs. 7,000 per bigha.
issues.conclusion: The later sale price of developed land did not justify higher compensation; the market value was fixed at Rs. 7,000 per bigha on the basis of the comparable determination for land acquired under the same notification.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 23 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, market value is assessed as at the date of publication of the Section 4(1) notification, with any proven acquisition-related damage also considered. Valuation may be based on expert opinion, bona fide comparable sales made within a reasonable time, or capitalisation and potential value. A later price for land after development does not establish its value at the acquisition date. In the absence of other evidence, the Court relied on the High Court's determination for land in the same village acquired under the same notification.

predicates.acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding challenges the compensation awarded for acquired land.
predicates.no_reliable_contemporaneous_valuation_ev: The claimant has not produced reliable evidence of market value near the acquisition notification date or other evidence supporting a higher value.
predicates.same_notification_comparable_determinati: A determination of market value exists for comparable land in the same locality acquired under the same notification.
predicates.later_high_price_reflects_development: The higher price relied on was obtained later, after the land had been developed.

issues.definition: When a compensation appeal lacks reliable contemporaneous valuation evidence but has a comparable determination for land acquired under the same notification, a later price reflecting development does not displace that comparable determination.

issues.legal_issue: Land acquired later in a nearby locality may receive the same compensation rate as land in a less distant locality where the court has upheld a lower-value finding for the former but awards the common rate in light of its later acquisition.
material_facts: The land in the farther locality was notified for acquisition 18 months after land in the less distant locality.
The Reference Court found, and the High Court upheld, that the farther locality's land had a lower market value because it was farther away.
The claimants did not show that the land in the farther locality had the same market value as the other land.
The High Court nevertheless awarded the same compensation rate, and the Supreme Court upheld that result and applied the enhanced rate of Rs. 7,000 per bigha.
issues.conclusion: The claimants whose land was in the farther locality were entitled to the same compensation rate of Rs. 7,000 per bigha as the land in the less distant locality.
issues.legal_principle: Market value is determined by the land's value at the relevant notification date and its location and advantages. The Court accepted the concurrent finding that the farther locality had a lower market value, but upheld the same compensation rate awarded for the locality notified earlier because the farther locality was notified later.

rule.if: acquisition_compensation_appeal and later_notified_locality and locality_is_farther and lower_value_finding_upheld

predicates.acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding challenges compensation awarded for acquired land.
predicates.later_notified_locality: The land in one locality was notified for acquisition after comparable land in another locality.
predicates.locality_is_farther: The court finds that the later-notified locality is farther from the relevant area or feature affecting value.
predicates.lower_value_finding_upheld: The finding that the later-notified locality's land had a lower market value is upheld.

issues.definition: When a compensation appeal concerns a farther locality notified later and its lower-value finding is upheld, the ruling gives it the same compensation rate as the earlier-notified locality.

issues.legal_issue: Eligible landowners must receive the amended statutory solatium and interest benefits on the compensation awarded.
material_facts: Some landowners had been awarded solatium at the rate applicable under the unamended provisions.
The Court held that they were entitled to solatium at 30 percent on the entire compensation, together with statutory interest payable under the amended provisions.
The Court also extended the statutory benefits to the enhanced compensation.
issues.conclusion: The landowners were entitled to 30 percent solatium on the entire compensation and to the applicable statutory interest under the amended Act, including on the enhanced amount.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the amended provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, as amended by Act 68 of 1984, concerning solatium and interest, and directed that the amended statutory benefits apply to the entire compensation, including the enhancement.

predicates.acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding challenges compensation awarded for acquired land.
predicates.amended_benefits_apply: The landowners are eligible for the statutory benefits introduced by the amended provisions.
predicates.prior_award_uses_unamended_solati​um: The prior award calculated solatium under the earlier, unamended provisions.

issues.definition: When an acquisition compensation appeal concerns landowners eligible for amended benefits whose prior award used the unamended solatium, the amended solatium and interest apply to the entire compensation.
